title: Book Three · Chapter 28: The Lid That Fits
story:
On Saturday, Ronan takes his finished reply to the post office. It tells Leo about the class photo and the family's plans for Sunday's walk. He asks about the winter visitors too.

He buys a stamp and sends this fourth letter. Then he reaches the tool shop a few minutes before ten.

The door is open, but the pavement is still quiet. He looks at the little parts in the window. Some screws are shorter than his fingernail.

Kai comes around the corner with his friend. They both have their collars up.

“Cold?” Ronan asks.

“Only outside my coat,” Kai says.

They walk toward the market. At the secondhand stall, Kai's friend stops to look at books. Kai finds a pile of old tins.

He wants one for the small parts in his drawer. He opens a blue tin, then a brown one.

“This is better.”

He puts the lid on. It will not close.

Ronan looks at the other tins. There is a brown lid under a red box.

“Try that.”

Kai changes the lids. This one fits. The blue lid fits the blue tin too.

The stallholder looks over.

“Someone mixed them up.”

Kai checks the bottom for holes. Then he asks the price and pays.

His friend puts a book back. He has not found the one he wants. The three boys move on.

At another stall, a man has small metal puzzles on a cloth. He holds up two rings. They are joined together.

“Can you separate these?” he asks.

Kai puts his tin under one arm and takes the rings. He turns them in his hands.

One ring has a narrow bend. Kai moves the other toward it, but it catches.

“Let me try,” his friend says.

He turns them the other way. They still catch.

Ronan takes them last. The metal feels cold. He finds a gap, pushes one ring through it, then stops.

Now the rings are stuck in a new place.

“Better?” Kai asks.

“Different.”

The man smiles and takes them back. His fingers turn once, then twice. The rings come apart.

All three boys lean closer.

“Again,” Kai says.

The man puts them together. This time Ronan watches the narrow bend. He sees the turn, but he is still not sure he can do it.

They thank the man and leave the rings on his cloth. Kai does not buy them. He still has his brown tin to carry home.

Near the corner, Ronan buys a small bag of roasted nuts. He opens it between the three of them.

Kai's friend takes one and cracks the shell.

“The puzzle was easier,” he says.

“You didn't do the puzzle,” Kai answers.

“I didn't do this either.”

He shows them the broken nut in his hand.

They laugh and walk back together. At West Lane, Ronan takes the empty paper bag from his pocket.

“I got my plan right,” he says.

“Food?”

“Food.”

Kai lifts the tin. “And I got a lid.”
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

lid＝盖子；stallholder＝摊主；separate＝分开；shell＝外壳、果壳。

## 理解问题

1. Kai最初为什么关不上棕色铁盒？Ronan怎样发现了问题？
2. 三个男孩有没有解开金属环？他们是不是必须买下才能离开？

## 读句子

**The metal feels cold.**

拆开看：The metal / feels / cold.

金属／摸起来／冰凉。
